stemMd:
Few official records of the 1890s postal service in the mountain town of Brask survive, so historian Celia Amundsen turned to an unusual source: the postmarks and handwritten notes on the backs of old envelopes. From these small marks she was able to ______ the routes that letters traveled, piecing together a map of the network one envelope at a time.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanationMd:
Look for the clue that defines what the blank must mean. The sentence ends by explaining it: Amundsen was "piecing together a map of the network one envelope at a time." She was rebuilding a picture of something that the missing records no longer showed directly.

**Reconstruct**, meaning to build up again from surviving pieces of evidence, matches that exactly.

Check the others by substituting them: she was not giving up on the routes, she was not announcing them to the public, and a historian studying old envelopes could not make the letters' routes any shorter.

distractorRationale.b: Abandon means to give up on something. The sentence says Amundsen succeeded in piecing together a map of the routes, the opposite of giving up on them.
distractorRationale.c: Publicize means to make widely known. The sentence is about how she worked the routes out from fragments, not about announcing them; nothing mentions an audience.
distractorRationale.d: Shorten would mean changing the routes themselves. A historian studying envelopes from the 1890s works out what the routes were; she cannot alter them.

accessibilityText: A short history passage. Few official records of the 1890s postal service in the mountain town of Brask survive, so historian Celia Amundsen turned to the postmarks and handwritten notes on the backs of old envelopes. From these small marks she was able to, blank, the routes that letters traveled, piecing together a map of the network one envelope at a time. Choose the word for the blank from reconstruct, abandon, publicize and shorten.

provenance.notes: Original words-in-context item. Brask, its postal service and Amundsen's study are invented; the closing participial phrase defines the blank.
